answers.answer: Open Commands, choose New command (or Make the first command on an empty list), enter schedule in Name, keep What it does at Sends a reply, and enter Tuesdays at 19:00 Amsterdam time. in Reply. Keep Twitch chat, Channel default and Starts with. Type !schedule in the channel's Twitch chat as broadcaster or platform moderator. UNKNOWN which action completes creation and whether the newly created command starts enabled: the numbered procedure goes directly from field choices to typing in chat. Later reference says an existing command can be switched on through its list switch or Enabled in the editor.
quote: Open Commands and choose New command. On an empty list, Make the first command opens the same dialog.
Enter schedule in Name.
Keep What it does at Sends a reply, and write your times in Reply. For example: Tuesdays at 19:00 Amsterdam time.
Keep Send the reply to at Twitch chat, Prefix at Channel default, and Match at Starts with.
Type !schedule in your channel’s Twitch chat as the broadcaster or a platform moderator.
Use the switch in its list row or Enabled at the top of its editor. Both save immediately, without Save changes.

answers.answer: Have the bot running, sign in, select the connected channel, and have its Twitch chat connection working. Moderator, Lead moderator, Editor or Broadcaster can change commands by default; the broadcaster may raise that requirement. A VIP given Commands access only has read-only access and cannot make the command. Test as broadcaster or platform moderator even offline; an ordinary viewer also needs a live stream or the offline setting enabled, permission and no cooldown.
quote: Have the bot running, sign in, and select your connected channel in the dashboard. The chat connection must work for the test below; use your connected Twitch chat for this first reply.
By default, a Moderator, Lead moderator, Editor or Broadcaster can open Commands and change commands. The broadcaster can raise the access requirement.

The broadcaster can also give VIPs list access through Permissions then Actions then Commands. That access is read-only: New command says “You can view this, but your role cannot change it.” The System commands tab is hidden.

Those accounts can test while you’re offline. An ordinary viewer needs the stream to be live, or Keep commands and rewards on while offline switched on, as well as permission to use the command and no active cooldown.

answers.answer: Open schedule, change Reply, and choose Save changes. The unsaved count disappearing and save button turning off confirm the save; typing the command again and seeing the new saved times in chat proves its result.
quote: To update your stream times, open schedule in the list and change Reply. The footer counts your edits, for example “1 unsaved change”.
Choose Save changes: the count disappears and the save button turns off. Type the command in chat again to see the new saved times.

answers.answer: The duplicate is welcome-copy, triggered with !welcome-copy using the usual prefix. It starts off and must be switched on before testing. It replies to Twitch chat, so choosing a destination is unnecessary unless another destination is wanted. Read it aloud is copied, but speech needs successful chat delivery and ready TTS. If the copy name exists, duplication is refused.
quote: Open a command and choose Duplicate in the footer. A copy of its saved settings opens with -copy after the name, for example !hello-copy.
The copy starts off, so switch it on before testing. Most settings are copied, including Read it aloud, but aliases, preset identity, reply destination and enabled state are not.
Aliases are additional names for the original command. The copy has no Reset to preset button and its reply goes to Twitch chat; you only need to choose a destination if you want a different one.
Speech still needs successful chat delivery and a ready TTS setup.
